TriCalculator.cos:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Returns the cosine approximation computed by Taylor expansion for x using 50 terms and rounds the result to 10 decimal places." cos]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> x </REF>: number "Input value to evaluate the cosine approximation for."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: number "The rounded cosine approximation."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Call self.taylor with x and the constant 50 to compute the Taylor-series approximation. RESULT taylor_value]
            [COMMAND Round taylor_value to 10 decimal places and return the rounded value. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
TriCalculator.factorial:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Compute a running product by multiplying descending values of a into b until a reaches 1, then return the accumulated result." factorial]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> a </REF>: number "The input value that is repeatedly multiplied into the accumulator while being decremented by 1 until it equals 1."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> b </REF>: number "The accumulated product after the loop finishes and the method returns."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize accumulator b to the constant value 1. RESULT b]
            [COMMAND While a is not equal to 1, multiply b by the current value of a. RESULT b]
            [COMMAND Within the same while loop iteration where a is not equal to 1, decrement a by 1. RESULT a]
            [COMMAND After the loop stops exactly when a equals 1, return b. RESULT return]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
TriCalculator.taylor:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Convert the input angle from degrees to radians, then build an alternating Taylor-series approximation by accumulating even-power terms up to n-1." taylor]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "Instance providing the factorial method and pi value access"
        <REF> x </REF>: number "Input angle in degrees, later converted to radians"
        <REF> n </REF>: integer "Upper bound for the series loop, iterating from 1 to n-1"
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: number "The accumulated Taylor-series approximation returned as a"
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Initialize a to 1, convert x from degrees to radians using x / 180 * pi, and initialize count to 1. RESULT a, x, count]
            [COMMAND For each k from 1 up to n - 1, evaluate whether count is odd by checking count % 2 != 0. RESULT parity_check]
            [COMMAND Within the loop, if count is odd, subtract (x ** (2 * k)) / self.factorial(2 * k) from a. RESULT a]
            [COMMAND Within the loop, if count is even, add (x ** (2 * k)) / self.factorial(2 * k) to a. RESULT a]
            [COMMAND After each loop iteration, increment count by 1 so the sign decision alternates on the next iteration. RESULT count]
            [COMMAND Return the final value of a after all iterations complete. RESULT a]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
TriCalculator.sin:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Converts an angle from degrees to radians, sums the sine series terms until the term magnitude falls below 1e-15, and returns the result rounded to 10 decimal places." sin]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> x </REF>: number "Angle in degrees."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: number "Sine of the angle, rounded to 10 decimal places."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Convert the input angle x from degrees to radians by computing x / 180 * pi. RESULT x]
            [COMMAND Initialize the running sum g to 0, set the first series term t to the converted x value, and initialize the term counter n to 1. RESULT g, t, n]
            [COMMAND While fabs(t) is at least 1e-15, add the current term t to g, increment n by 1, and update t using the recurrence -t * x * x / (2 * n - 1) / (2 * n - 2). RESULT g, t, n]
            [COMMAND Return g rounded to 10 decimal places. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
TriCalculator.tan:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Computes tangent as sine divided by cosine, rounded to 10 decimal places, and returns False when cosine is zero to avoid division by zero." tan]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> self </REF>: object "Instance providing sin(x) and cos(x) methods."
        <REF> x </REF>: number "Input angle or value passed to trigonometric functions."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: number|bool "Rounded tangent-like value to 10 decimal places, or False when cosine is zero."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Evaluate self.cos(x) and test whether it is not equal to 0. RESULT cos_value_nonzero]
            [COMMAND If self.cos(x) is not 0, compute result as self.sin(x) divided by self.cos(x). RESULT result]
            [COMMAND Within the nonzero cosine branch, return round(result, 10). RESULT return_value]
            [COMMAND If self.cos(x) is 0, return False immediately. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: self.cos(x) equals 0]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Skip the division and rounding step to avoid division by zero. RESULT skipped_computation]
            [COMMAND Return False as the fallback value. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
